frames.title: What Is Desire
frames.on_screen:
What Is Desire
The force that makes advertising work.

Desires are defined as a strong feeling of wishing for something. A desire is related to both needs and wants of people.

Desire is the demand that already exists and is flowing through the market.

You CAN NOT create desire, you can only channel it.

Easy A Media

frames.title: Types Of Desire In The Market
frames.on_screen:
Types Of Desire In The Market
The force that makes advertising work.

There are 2 types of main desires that exist in the market
Permanent Desire - Health, Wealth, Relationships (Desires that never leave us)
Trending Desire - Crypto, Valentines Day, AI (Desires that come and go)

THE 3 MARKETS
Diagram showing three intersecting circles labeled: Wealth, Health, Relationships
Easy A Media

frames.title: Desire Strength: Tailwind Concept
frames.on_screen:
Desire Strength
The force that makes advertising work.

The strength of your desire will determine the success of your ad.

Your goal is to find the dominant desire based on:
Intensity -> Minor headache VS severe migraine
Scope -> The total amount of people that share the desire

Diagram showing an airplane labeled "= Your Ad"
Below: "Strong Desire" runway diagram showing an airplane flying along a dashed line with a red arrow behind it labeled "Tailwind"

frames.title: Types Of Desire On Your Product
frames.on_screen:
Types Of Desire On Your Product
The force that makes advertising work.

The product you sell is actually 2 products. Your customer purchases what the product DOES (functional) The physical only justifies the price or documents the quality.

The Physical - Carbon fiber, wires, motherboard
The Functional - shiny, smooth, celebrity style hair

Physical (images of button, carbon fiber texture, circuit board)
The Product (hairdryer)
Functional (photo of celebrity hairstyling session)

Easy A Media

frames.title: How To Find Mass Desire And Ad Angle Examples
frames.on_screen:
How To Find Mass Desire
The force that makes advertising work.

Research - Look for "I wanted", "I was looking for", "I was in need"
Testing - Testing each desire inside of your Ad creatives & messaging

"Find a style" VS "I want to look wealthy"

Ad example 1: Just Men Shoes - "Find your style"
Ad example 2: Just Men Shoes - "Look like a million bucks. Spend WAY less than that... If These Shoes Were Sold in Macy's or Nordstrom They Would Cost $250+"
Ad example 3 (video ad): BRRRN - "BRRRN CALORIES, TRANSFORM YOUR BOOTY!"

Easy A Media
